name: Early Christian Monuments of Ravenna
description: Ravenna, in northern Italy's Emilia-Romagna region, was capital of the Western Roman Empire in the 5th century and later of Byzantine Italy. Eight churches, baptisteries and tombs from the 5th and 6th centuries survive, their interiors glittering with gold and jewel-coloured mosaics. Visitors can see Christ, saints and emperors rendered in tiny glass tiles, which have earned the city its title "capital of mosaics".
